subject: Post-demo recap: model recommendations, retrieval params, and eval pack
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@clearlinehealth.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-31T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo recap: model recommendations, retrieval params, and eval pack

Thanks again for taking the demo today — really appreciated the detailed walkthrough of Clearline's knowledge base and the types of decision-support questions care managers ask. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we can get you a focused RAG eval kit this week.

High-level fit: from what you showed, primary goals are:
- Accurate grounding for clinical SOPs and policy docs (short, high-precision answers)
- Good multi-doc synthesis for case summaries (concise + provenance)
- Low hallucination tolerance on dosing/triage content (must hit grounding metric thresholds)

Model candidates (to include in the eval):
1) Llama2-13B-chat (q4f) — good latency/cost balance, strong instruction-following for summarization tasks.
2) Mistral-Instruct-7B (fp16) — faster endpoints, slightly lower param count; useful for read-heavy paths where you can rely on a strong reranker.
3) Redwood-verified-rlhf-13B (fp16) — higher quality baseline for synthesis; include for sanity checks on regression.

RAG / retrieval suggestions to test:
- Embedding model: text-embed-3 (semantic first pass)
- Retriever: dense semantic with a small BM25 backstop; test both top_k=8 and top_k=16 sweeps
- Chunking: 512-token chunks, 64-token overlap (documents tend to have many small sections)
- Reranker: compare a cross-encoder re-ranker (crossenc-rank-v2) vs a lightweight pairwise (poly-rank-small) for latency/cost tradeoffs.

Suggested metrics we'll include in the eval pack:
- Grounding precision@k (fraction of answers that cite a correct doc/span)
- Hallucination rate on the clinical test set (binary scoring)
- Response latency (p50/p95) at 5 qps and 25 qps
- Cost per 1k tokens + per-call reranker cost estimate

Attachments and what they contain:
- clearline_eval_promptset_v1.zip: initial prompt templates + 35 gold test prompts derived from today's call
- retrieval-config-suggested.yaml: the retrieval/re-ranking configs we propose as starting points
- reranker-comparison-brief.pdf: short note on tradeoffs and expected cost deltas

Immediate next steps (proposed):
1) You confirm the three model candidates and we provision a short eval bundle (3 models x 2 retrieval configs).
2) Clearline sends a representative 300–500 doc slice (can be anonymized) or we pull a sample via secure S3 link.
3) We run a 48–72 hour smoke evaluation, then share a dashboard and call to review the grounding metrics.

I'll loop Marcus in to head up the reranker experiments once you confirm sample availability. Happy to adapt if you prefer different model candidates.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: clearline_eval_promptset_v1.zip (archive)]

From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@clearlinehealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Clearline Health Sales Ops <supportops@clearlinehealth.com>
Date: 2027-10-31T17:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: model recommendations, retrieval params, and eval pack

Thanks Sean — this is great and aligned with what our clinical leads asked for. A few clarifying notes: 
- Confirm we will not run any patient-identifiable data through the hosted sandbox; we'll provide an anonymized S3 bucket.
- For the test prompts in the pack: can you add a few negative examples (incorrect/cross-document traps) so we can stress hallucination detection?

Model choices look reasonable. Preference order from our side: Redwood-verified-rlhf-13B (best-quality baseline) > Llama2-13B-chat > Mistral-Instruct-7B. But also sensitive to cost; we'll want a cost estimate per 10k queries.

We can get you a 400-document anonymized sample by EOD Wednesday. Please include a simple NDA addendum (one paragraph) that clarifies evaluation-only retention.

Ellen Park
Head of Product, Clearline Health
[Phone: (415) 555-0291]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@clearlinehealth.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-01T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: model recommendations, retrieval params, and eval pack

Thanks Ellen — we'll treat the S3 sample as the canonical eval corpus (anonymized works fine). A few tech specifics so the team knows what we'll spin up: 

Retrieval configs we'll run in parallel (two lanes):
- lane A (semantic-first): embedding=text-embed-3, store=dense-hnsw, top_k_retriever=16, chunk_size=512, overlap=64, reranker=crossenc-rank-v2 (p95 cost higher)
- lane B (bm25-backstop): bm25+semantic hybrid, top_k_retriever=8, chunk_size=512, overlap=64, reranker=poly-rank-small (cheaper, lower latency)

Reranker experiment plan: we'll run a head-to-head on a 100-prompt subset measuring grounding-precision@3, latency delta, and per-call cost. If crossenc precision > poly by >8% and latency within your SLA, we'll recommend crossenc for critical paths and poly for lower-cost endpoints.

Prompt set notes: Sean's pack looks good — I'll add 12 intentionally adversarial prompts (traps/contradictions) and include annotation instructions for your clinical SMEs.

Docs we will upload to the shared drive: retrieval-config-suggested.yaml, reranker-comparison-brief.pdf. Both attached here for reference.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Lead ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: retrieval-config-suggested.yaml]
[Attachment: reranker-comparison-brief.pdf]

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: model recommendations, retrieval params, and eval pack

Perfect — thanks Ellen and Marcus. Quick checklist to keep momentum: 
- Ellen: S3 anonymized sample (400 docs) + short NDA addendum request (we'll send a one-paragraph addendum this afternoon).
- Redwood: provision eval bundle (3 models x 2 retrieval lanes) and run the 48–72h smoke; we'll prioritize the 100-prompt reranker head-to-head and share an early dashboard link.
- Timeline: expect provisional results and dashboard by end of day Thursday (48 hours from start).

I'll send the NDA addendum and the HubSpot link for the deal. Looking forward to the run — will loop in Solutions Eng if we need custom ingest code.

—Sean
